text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said he was ready for any lawsuit by opposition politician Tang Liang Hong over his comments that the opposition leader is a "Chinese chauvinist" for criticising the presence of too many Christian-educated ministers and permanent secretaries in the government.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said the views of Mr Tang reflect a dangerous line threatening racial harmony in multi-racial and multi-religious Singapore.

- Opposition candidate Tang Liang Hong denied that he delivered a statement two years ago criticising the presence of too many Christian-educated and English-speaking ministers and permanent secretaries in the government. He said the PAP was trying to frighten voters to prevent them from electing him to Parliament.
- The first direct talks between Marxist rebels and the Peruvian government led to the release of 20 new hostages. About 83 hostages were still being held captive by the guerrillas.
- The government's Department of Statistics said a survey showed that department stores and supermarkets reported higher sales in 1994, but profit margins were badly squeezed by keen competition.

- Swiss-based Allseas Group is asking for Singapore $649.5 million if it wins a court case over a 1993 contract involving its vessel, Solitaire, against Sembawang Corp, which in turn is claiming S$231.2 million in damages from Allseas for wrongful termination of the contract.
- DBS Bank has promoted Mr Ng Kee Choe to president and Mr. Tan Soo Nan to deputy president, effective on January 1.

- Publicly-listed Creative Technology and Powermatic Data Systems are among a handful of Singapore companies eyeing the market for Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line (ASDL) line cards, which deliver data at high speed over existing phone lines.

- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said the threat by opposition politician Tang Liang Hong to take them to court over their views that he is an extremist represent an attempt to sidestep the debate on his character.
- U.S. stock mutual fund investors poured US$3.56 billion into mutual funds in the six days ending on Christmas eve, the largest since November 20, estimates by AMG Data Services said.
- The sale of ST Computer Systems' simulator and command and control businesses to ST Electronics and Engineering will improve the formers' net tangible asset values, Bankers' Trust Company said.
- DBS Bank said Ng Kee Choe is the new president, filling a year-long vacancy, to oversee the entire bank's operations. The appointment takes effect on January 1.
